## Source 1 — arXiv 2508.04721: "Toward Low-Latency End-to-End Voice Agents for Telecommunications Using Streaming ASR, Quantized LLMs, and Real-Time TTS" (NetoAI)

**Type:** arXiv preprint (Aug 2025)
**Engagement signal:** High — the canonical "low-latency voice agent" engineering paper for 2025-2026
**Headline:** "Toward Low-Latency End-to-End Voice Agents for Telecommunications Using Streaming ASR, Quantized LLMs, and Real-Time TTS"

### Verbatim excerpts (from abstract):
> "We introduce a low-latency telecom AI voice agent pipeline for real-time, interactive telecommunications use, enabling advanced voice AI for call center automation, intelligent IVR (Interactive Voice Response), and AI-driven customer support. The solution is built for telecom, combining four specialized models by NetoAI: TSLAM, a 4-bit quantized Telecom-Specific Large Language Model (LLM); T-VEC, a Telecom-Specific Embedding Model; TTE, a Telecom-Specific Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) model; and T-Synth, a Te..."

### Pain points (verbatim engineering language):
- "low-latency" — the recurring design constraint
- "4-bit quantized" — the quantization cost-vs-accuracy trade-off
- "Telecom-Specific" — the domain-tuning pattern (general models lose on jargon; specialized models win on it)
- "Streaming ASR" — the partial-transcript pattern (start LLM inference before the user finishes speaking)

### Why this works:
This is the engineering anchor for the persona's "Dre Builds" build. The 4-model split (LLM + embedding + ASR + TTS) is the modern voice-agent architecture; the 4-bit quantization is the cost-engineering pattern that makes sub-700ms economically viable. The Pillar 4 angle: "Here's the architecture paper that justifies the sub-700ms target. Here's the build log showing we hit it. The math is the product." The voice: a 4-bullet spec dump + the actual number we hit.

## Source 2 — arXiv 2601.19952: "LTS-VoiceAgent: A Listen-Think-Speak Framework for Efficient Streaming Voice Interaction via Semantic Triggering and Incremental Reasoning"

**Type:** arXiv preprint (Jan 2026)
**Headline:** "LTS-VoiceAgent: A Listen-Think-Speak Framework for Efficient Streaming Voice Interaction via Semantic Triggering and Incremental Reasoning"

### Verbatim excerpts (from abstract):
> "Real-time voice agents face a dilemma: end-to-end models often lack deep reasoning, while cascaded pipelines incur high latency by executing ASR, LLM reasoning, and TTS strictly in sequence, unlike human conversation where listeners often start thinking before the speaker finishes. Since cascaded architectures remain the dominant choice for complex tasks, existing cascaded streaming strategies attempt to reduce this latency via mechanical segmentation (e.g., fixed ch..."

### Pain points:
- "end-to-end models lack deep reasoning" — the cascade-vs-end-to-end trade-off
- "human conversation where listeners often start thinking before the speaker finishes" — the bio-inspired framing
- "mechanical segmentation" — the brute-force approach that doesn't work
- "Semantic Triggering" — the pattern that does work (start inference when the LLM has enough semantic signal, not when the ASR is "done")

### Why this works:
This is the "human conversation as the latency budget" frame. The persona's sub-700ms target is grounded in this: the human conversation overlap is the floor, the cascade architecture is the ceiling unless you do incremental reasoning. The Pillar 4 build log would call this out as "the reason we don't wait for the ASR to finalize before firing the LLM." The voice: "The LLM doesn't wait. The user doesn't notice. The latency floor is human conversation, not 700ms."
